chapter: Boston roadhouses and the Army band
title: Troopship to France, the torpedo scare and the wet camp
summary: He describes the convoy, being seasick when the ship was thought torpedoed, meeting shell-shocked soldiers and marching in rainy France.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So then we went to France from Fort Dix and when we landed in France, San Jose --

We went over and we had a convoy see and we got about a couple days out, the convoy left us and the -- you could hear the water slushing against the outside of the ship and one day the lights went out. Now we're six decks down and I was seasick and the smell of the ship made me seasick and I was in my bunk, what do you call, the hammock and the cat hollered 'Oh, we're torpedoed,' and they all made a rush and here

I'm sick, I can't move and they all run up and then afterwhile the lights come back on so afterwhile I said to the guy, where do you think you're going. You're six decks down and we were torpedoed how are you going to get out. You can't get out. You're six decks down.

So then we landed in St. Jose (?) and I met a whole lot of the guys that were what do you call it, they were shell shocked over there, the Eighth Illinois. And they didn't know anything. They were vacant, had a vacant stare and they were gassed, you know.

And then we went to the camp, they call it sunny France, but it rained every day we were over there and you march all day long and you put your pup tent up and at night it would rain again and you'd have a wet blanket, oh, they were all wet and I remember we marched to -- I got in the band, see.
